result.title: Dream-COP: Guiding Algorithm Discovery for Combinatorial Optimization Problems in an Experience World
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) enable algorithm discovery for combinatorial optimization problems (COPs) through iterative program generation and evaluation. A central challenge is how to organize search to discover better algorithms within a limited budget. Our key insight is that past search trajectories and their recorded outcomes form an experience world, which can be used to facilitate the COP solving through replay. We introduce Dream-COP, in which a \emph{policy agent} learns executable policies through \emph{dreaming} in this experience world to guide a \emph{discovery agent} in generating and refining COP programs. Specifically, policy replay provides feedback on the quality of the programs revealed and the search steps used, to guide policy selection more effectively. Across five COPs, \textsc{Dream} discovers better algorithms than fixed exploration in both heuristic component design and complete solver generation. Particularly, it matches the optimal values on KP and reduces the gap on OBPP from 2.112\% to 1.199\% while using 42.5\% fewer search requests. Moreover, the learned exploration policies transfer effectively across different COPs with the assitance of the experience world.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Dream-COP：把历史搜索轨迹及其结果构成「经验世界」，通过在其中回放训练 policy agent 学得可执行的探索策略，用来指导 discovery agent 生成与改进组合优化程序，在五个 COP 上用更少搜索请求取得更优算法。
AI.relevance_reason: 其以回放经验学习「如何探索、如何分配搜索预算」的策略，可能为 LVR 的动态计算、停止决策与轨迹训练的信用分配提供类比线索，但能否迁移到多模态推理状态仍需核查。
